# Leeway

> Leeway is a free, open-source Chrome extension that shows how much of your Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini usage limits is left — the 5-hour and weekly limits — as a percentage with reset times, in a popup, the toolbar badge and an always-on-top overlay. Unofficial; not affiliated with Anthropic, OpenAI or Google.

## What it does
- Shows the remaining percentage and reset time of each usage limit, as the signed-in usage pages show them (not a token-count estimate). A value that could not be read is shown as "?", never as 0%.
- Toolbar badge with the lowest remaining value among the enabled services, color-coded (green from 50, orange 20–49, red below 20, grey when stale).
- Always-on-top floating overlay through Chrome's Document Picture-in-Picture (Chrome 116+), opened from a small Leeway window (popup: Open overlay, then Float on top or Enter), collapsible to one line.
- Plan names (e.g. Max 5x, Plus) when the service reports them; every Claude organization of one sign-in shown separately.
- Refreshes every 2 minutes; UI in English, Korean, Spanish, Japanese, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional).

## Supported services
- Claude (claude.ai): 5-hour and weekly limits, read in the background from the usage endpoint claude.ai's usage page uses.
- ChatGPT (chatgpt.com): what Settings > Usage shows — the plan limits shared by Codex, Work, workspace agents and ChatGPT for Excel (5-hour, weekly or 30-day depending on the account). Ordinary chat conversations are not counted there.
- Gemini (gemini.google.com): read from an open gemini.google.com/usage tab; that page must be open. The popup's "Gemini usage" button opens that page, or switches to it if it is already open, and reads it once it has loaded.

## Privacy
- Uses the sessions already signed in to in Chrome. No sign-in, and no cookie, password or API key to paste.
- Session tokens are never stored, logged or transmitted. Conversations are never read.
- No server, no account, no analytics; data stays in the browser (chrome.storage.local).
- Site permissions are optional and requested per service when it is turned on.

## Several accounts
- Separate accounts: one Chrome profile per account. On Windows, the optional and experimental Leeway helper (leeway-helper.exe, GitHub Releases) lets each profile show the others' remaining usage, through a local file only.
